title: Simplify multi-tenant lookup graphs and add query metrics pipeline
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: The control plane contains multiple overlapping lookup paths used to resolve tenant metadata (tenant -> workspace -> resource -> policy). Over time we accumulated denormalized columns, shadow FK columns, and two different materialized view strategies. This causes confusing query plans, hotspots for API read paths, and makes index ownership unclear. Work here intends to rationalize those lookup graphs into a single canonical set of views and indexes, remove deprecated columns, and add a light-weight query metrics pipeline that surfaces expensive queries so we can iterate on index choices without guesswork.

Goals: 1) Standardize the multi-tenant lookup layer so the most common API read paths hit the same set of indexed relations. 2) Remove three deprecated columns (tenant_name_v1, workspace_ref_legacy, resource_shadow_id) and consolidate FK references to canonical UUIDs. 3) Introduce a nightly job that aggregates slow-query samples and query plans into a metrics table/dashboards. 4) Achieve meaningful p95 latency improvements on control-plane reads for the tenant resolution paths (target: 30% p95 reduction) and reduce CPU spikes during high concurrency.

Scope: schema modifications (safe additive where possible), concurrent indexes, backfill jobs for normalized FK columns, controlled column drop cadence (mark -> wait -> drop), migration SQL scripts, monitoring and dashboards, and runbook for rollback and emergency mitigation.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical lookup views created and referenced by API codepaths (runtime flags available)
All reads for /v1/tenants/:id and internal tenant resolution use canonical UUID columns in 90% of traffic by end of rollout
Deprecated columns marked as deprecated in metadata and dropped in a follow-up once no traffic uses them
New nightly query-metrics table populated and available in Grafana with top-50 slow control-plane queries
No sustained replication lag > 30s during migration windows and no application errors caused by schema changes
migration_plan: Phase 0 - Prep: add new canonical_uuid columns (nullable) and write code path behind feature flag to populate from existing joins
Phase 1 - Backfill: run controlled backfills in tenant-day batches using background workers; monitor replication lag and CPU
Phase 2 - Indexing: create concurrent indexes on canonical columns and the new canonical materialized view; validate query plans
Phase 3 - Switch: flip feature flags for read paths to prefer canonical views and index-backed joins; monitor for regressions
Phase 4 - Quarantine: mark old columns as deprecated (DB comment + annotation), leave for 8 weeks, then schedule drop window with on-call coverage
Phase 5 - Remove: drop deprecated columns and legacy materialized artifacts in a low-traffic maintenance window
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Long-running backfills cause replication lag or table bloat. Mitigation: throttle backfills, process tenant groups, and monitor PG replication stats.
Risk: Index creation still takes locks on high-volume tables. Mitigation: use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY and perform on read replicas when possible, use PG 13+ safety checks.
Risk: Application reads go to old paths during partial rollout. Mitigation: use feature flags, ensure fallback behavior, and spike test in staging with shadow traffic.
Risk: Query-metrics pipeline increases write volume. Mitigation: aggregate samples and cap retained samples per query key, roll out at 1% then 10% before full enablement.
progress_updates: 2026-01-12: Ticket opened. Initial spike found 4 denormalized columns that are safe to migrate. Identified top-3 offending queries via existing pganalyze reports.
2026-01-19: Prototype view implemented in staging; observed 25% p95 improvement on synthetic tenant reads. Shared draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4123
2026-01-26: Backfill tool landed as background worker with throttling knobs. Began small-sample backfills on staging and observed no replication lag.
2026-02-02: Nightly query-metrics job committed (aggregates slow queries and EXPLAIN plans); dashboard skeleton created: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/CPDB/slow-queries
2026-02-05: Began controlled backfills for 150 production tenants overnight (low-traffic region). Monitoring dashboard shows stable replication and modest CPU increase (+8%).
